comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C6, C41-C43, C101. Both evaluations find the foxj1a rescue experiments well-supported and elegant. Peer review explicitly praises this as a strength, while OpenEval notes strong evidence for cell-type-specific requirement.

Perfect agreement on claims C7, C60-C63, C107. Both evaluations support the conclusion that Urp1/2 upregulation is not a main driver of scoliosis. Peer review explicitly praises this as an 'elegant genetic demonstration,' matching OpenEval's assessment of well-supported negative genetic interaction results.

Perfect agreement on claims C9-C10, C75-C79, C84-C86 regarding astrogliosis and Annexin A2 upregulation. Both find the evidence well-supported. Peer review describes this as 'very interesting finding' that may inform pathogenic mechanisms, while OpenEval notes the temporal relationship suggesting astrogliosis precedes scoliosis.

Perfect agreement on claims C80-C83 regarding immune cell recruitment. Both evaluations support the findings of increased LCP1+ cells and correlation with GFAP staining. Peer review acknowledges neuroinflammatory response, while OpenEval notes the dynamic temporal pattern requires further investigation.

Perfect agreement on claims C14, C94-C100 regarding cep290 mutant phenotypes. Both evaluations support the finding that cep290 shows similar astrogliosis and immune phenotypes as rpgrip1l. Peer review acknowledges comprehensive characterization of both mutants, matching OpenEval's assessment of generalizability.

Perfect agreement on claims C44-C45 regarding SEM evidence of cilia organization differences. Both evaluations support these observations as part of comprehensive characterization, with no concerns raised about validity.

Strong agreement on claims C11-C13, C87-C93 regarding NACET treatment effects. Both evaluations support the findings. Peer review provides 'convincing evidence' for neuroinflammation role, while OpenEval notes correlation supports but doesn't prove causation. Peer review notes the approach is not novel but results are valid.

Strong agreement on claims C2, C37-C40 regarding scoliosis phenotype characterization. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review describes 'comprehensive characterization' with no concerns, while OpenEval notes converging evidence with high penetrance. OpenEval also includes C35-C36 not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Agreement on claims C3, C54 regarding ventricular enlargement. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review acknowledges this as a strength allowing identification of phenotypes correlated with spine curvature, matching OpenEval's assessment of established temporal relationship. OpenEval includes C53 not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Both address the main mechanistic conclusion (C15, C115) but with critical difference. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting correlation is established but causal mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating authors 'do not formally demonstrate that these events are sufficient to drive spine curvature' and that 'functional consequences remain uncertain.'

Agreement on claims C4, C55-C56, C59 regarding Reissner fiber loss correlation with scoliosis. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review acknowledges this as a strength but notes it's 'already well established in literature.' OpenEval includes additional claims C5, C51-C52 about MCC loss that peer review addresses separately.

Partial overlap on claims C5, C51-C52 regarding MCC loss at posterior SCO. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review acknowledges cilia loss correlation with spine curvature as part of comprehensive analysis, noting it's established in literature but not challenging validity.

Agreement on claims C8, C64-C69 regarding transcriptomic findings. Both evaluations support the data. Peer review acknowledges increased Annexin A2 expression and astrogliosis as key findings, while OpenEval notes comprehensive data but causal relationship requires validation. Peer review notes neuroinflammation previously identified in other models.

Partial overlap on proteomic data (C70-C74). OpenEval addresses proteomics specifically with quantitative thresholds and Annexin family enrichment. Peer review addresses transcriptomic and protein expression together, acknowledging Annexin A2 findings as part of broader astrogliosis characterization.

Strong overlap on claims C46-C50 regarding cilia defects characterization. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review acknowledges 'very clear and comprehensive analysis' including cilia defects and ventricular dilations. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements and lack of correlation between some defects and curvature status.

Partial overlap on claims C35-C36 regarding lack of early embryonic defects. Both evaluations support these observations as part of comprehensive phenotypic characterization. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings, while OpenEval explicitly includes them in scoliosis phenotype characterization.

OpenEval addresses SCO-spondin aggregate distribution (C57-C58) as supported but notes functional significance remains unclear. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses established literature context (C1, C16-C34) as appropriately cited background knowledge. Peer review does not separately evaluate literature citations but implicitly accepts them as context.

OpenEval addresses additional established literature (C102, C104-C114, C116-C117) used for contextualization as appropriately cited. Peer review does not separately evaluate these literature citations.
